source_note: Cost ranges compiled from national contractor survey data (HomeAdvisor, Angi, RSMeans). Actual costs vary by region, home age, and material choices. Get 3 quotes for jobs over $500.

repairs.name: Fix dripping faucet
repairs.tip: Identify faucet type first — cartridge vs compression vs ball requires different parts.

repairs.name: Replace toilet flapper
repairs.tip: Universal flappers fit most toilets. Bring the old flapper to the store to match size.

repairs.name: Unclog a drain
repairs.tip: Try a drain snake before chemicals. Most bathroom clogs are hair just below the stopper.

repairs.name: Fix low water pressure
repairs.tip: Check and clean faucet aerators first — often the entire fix costs under $5.

repairs.name: Replace bathtub drain
repairs.tip: A drain removal tool ($15) makes it easy. Use plumber's putty, not caulk, around the drain flange.

repairs.name: Replace leaky outdoor faucet
repairs.tip: Shut off the interior valve first. Frost-free sillcocks are worth the extra cost in cold climates.

repairs.name: Replace light switch
repairs.tip: Always kill the circuit at the breaker and verify with a voltage tester before touching any wire.

repairs.name: Replace electrical outlet
repairs.tip: Match the amperage: 15A outlets on 15A circuits, 20A (T-slot) on 20A circuits.

repairs.name: Install GFCI outlet
repairs.tip: One GFCI can protect all downstream outlets on the same circuit via the LOAD terminals.

repairs.name: Replace ceiling light fixture
repairs.tip: Verify the existing box is rated for the fixture weight before hanging a heavy chandelier.

repairs.name: Install programmable thermostat
repairs.tip: Photograph the existing wiring before disconnecting anything. Label each wire with tape.

repairs.name: Patch small drywall hole
repairs.tip: Self-adhesive patches work for holes under 4 inches. Feather mud in thin coats — 3 thin beats 1 thick.

repairs.name: Repair large drywall section
repairs.tip: Cut to the nearest studs for solid backing. Use a California patch for mid-wall repairs.

repairs.name: Tape and mud drywall
repairs.tip: Joint compound shrinks as it dries. Let each coat dry completely before applying the next.

repairs.name: Repair water-damaged ceiling
repairs.tip: Fix the leak source before repairing drywall — otherwise the damage will return.

repairs.name: Paint a room
repairs.tip: Spend 60% of your time on prep. Paint quality matters more than technique.

repairs.name: Paint over water stain
repairs.tip: Shellac or oil-based stain-blocking primer is essential. Latex primer will not stop stains from bleeding through.

repairs.name: Paint a brick fireplace
repairs.tip: Use masonry primer and masonry-rated latex. Painting brick is permanent — limewash is reversible if you want a softer look.

repairs.name: Paint trim without brush strokes
repairs.tip: Thin latex trim paint slightly with Floetrol. Use a high-quality angled sash brush and don't overwork the paint.

repairs.name: Recaulk bathtub
repairs.tip: Fill the tub with water before caulking so the joint is at max width. Remove all old caulk completely first.

repairs.name: Fix door that won't latch
repairs.tip: The strike plate is almost always the culprit — loosen and shift it 1/8 inch before reaching for a chisel.

repairs.name: Fix sticking door
repairs.tip: Check hinges first. A loose hinge screw causes most sticking doors. Longer screws into the stud frame solve it cheaply.

repairs.name: Install deadbolt lock
repairs.tip: ANSI Grade 1 deadbolts cost $20–$30 more than Grade 3 and are worth it for exterior doors.

repairs.name: Replace window weatherstripping
repairs.tip: V-strip (tension seal) weatherstripping outperforms foam tape in durability. A $10 roll covers several windows.

repairs.name: Replace damaged laminate plank
repairs.tip: Buy extra planks at install time. Manufacturers discontinue patterns and matching years later is hard.

repairs.name: Clean and restore grout
repairs.tip: Oxygen bleach outperforms grout-specific cleaners at a fraction of the cost. Seal grout after cleaning.

repairs.name: Fix loose tile
repairs.tip: If the tile is not cracked, injecting construction adhesive under it is faster than a full reset.

repairs.name: Level floor before tiling
repairs.tip: Self-leveling compound is beginner-friendly for small dips. Grind high spots first before pouring.

repairs.name: Repair concrete walkway
repairs.tip: Use polymer-modified concrete mix — it bonds better to existing concrete than plain mix.

repairs.name: Repair brick mortar joints
repairs.tip: Rake joints to 3/4-inch depth before repointing. Shallow mortar pops out within a season.

repairs.name: Install mailbox post
repairs.tip: Set the post in concrete and let cure 24 hours. Mailbox should sit 41–45 inches above road surface.
